transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood PM), Carlos (OrbitFlow CTO), Ava (Platform Eng), Tom (Product), Nina (Security)

--- Summary / Purpose: align on runbook and quant pipeline for marketplace listing + finalize operational playbooks and demo benchmark approach.

00:00:03 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and we want to make sure by the end we have clear owners for the runbook and the benchmark plan.
00:00:18 Carlos: hey, yep thanks. We're hoping to get marketplace listing done end of month, need clarity on manifest, signing, and what you need from our side.
00:00:30 Liam: great. I'm Liam, I'm going to lead the bench side, we'll test int8 and fp16 variants and the fallback routing.
00:00:38 Ava: quick heads up, our infra uses a private subnet plus a customer-managed KMS - we'll need the allowlist and some guidance on HSM if required.
00:00:50 Maya: noted, and Nina from security will be useful for that.

00:01:12 Tom: first question, when you say "manifest signing" what exactly do you need? Is that a signature we host, or a file we sign then upload?
00:01:24 Priya: good question, Priya here — short answer: we provide a signing workflow template. You can sign manifests with your KMS key or use Redwood's notarization for marketplace. We need to capture preference in the runbook.
00:01:40 Nina: our compliance team will insist on customer-key-first approach, so we need KMS-integration steps documented and any attestation artifacts.

00:02:15 Liam: on the quant pipeline, we propose a staged flow: fp16 baseline, int8 calibration with representative dataset, then run throughput runs under realistic qps. We'll measure latency p50/p95/p99 and token-per-second, and also evaluate hallucination/regression on the evaluation set.
00:02:38 Carlos: we've got a 2M-row conversational sample, but it's redacted. Is that ok for calibration?
00:02:46 Liam: yes that's actually good. We'll need a small sample for regen tests too (1000-2k prompts).

00:03:10 Speaker 2 (may be Maya): walk through network topology for private deployment - do you want diagrams?
00:03:18 Ava: yes diagrams are helpful, we run egress rules through a firewall, so we'll need TCP allowlist to Redwood's ingestion endpoints, and we prefer an S3-compatible object store for logs.
00:03:30 Maya: we'll provide a template diagram and the allowlist IP ranges. Note: sometimes the geo IP ranges change, we'll call out the tag to watch.

00:04:05 Tom: cost - how much higher is int8 vs fp16? I assume int8 cheaper but more ops in calibration?
00:04:16 Liam: cost is typically lower for int8 at inference time — about 20-45% lower token cost depending on kernel and batch. Calibration has an upfront cost but is one-off. But watch for accuracy regressions, so you may keep fp16 for critical routes.
00:04:35 Carlos: can we set routing policies? like sensitive customer route uses fp16, everything else int8?
00:04:45 Maya: yes, Smart routing can do per-route policies. In the runbook we show a canary route that pins to fp16 for 5% of traffic then expands to 30% etc.

00:05:10 Ava: observability — what metrics should we instrument?
00:05:16 Liam: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-second, model variant tag, quantization variant tag (int8/fp16), prefix cache hit rate, and a small set of quality metrics (ROUGE-ish or custom eval score) reported asynchronously. Also span tags for request id and route.
00:05:35 Priya: and we'll include example Grafana dashboards and exported traces.

00:06:02 Carlos: about manifest signing again, do you support OCI image signatures or is this custom?
00:06:12 Maya: we support signing the manifest artifact (not necessarily OCI) and can integrate with Cosign if you prefer. We'll add step-by-step for Cosign + KMS.

00:06:55 Nina: security asks: where are logs retained? retention period? are they encrypted-at-rest with customer keys?
00:07:05 Maya: standard: logs encrypted at rest, and for Private deployments we can wire to your KMS. Retention is configurable; for marketplace listing, we document default 30 days and add a compliance section for longer retention.

00:07:36 Tom: can you walk through the canary rollback triggers? I want explicit thresholds.
00:07:45 Liam: sure — our recommended triggers: 1) p95 latency increases by >30% over baseline for 3 minutes, 2) error rate >1% (5xx or model inference exceptions) for 2 minutes, 3) quality metric drop >5% on evaluation set for two consecutive checks. If any trigger fires, route back to previous variant and notify on-call.
00:08:12 Ava: do you do automatic rollback or manual?
00:08:18 Liam: we support both. For marketplace we normally recommend manual confirmation for safety, but for internal dedicated pools customers can enable automatic fallback. We'll capture both options in runbook.

00:09:00 Carlos: about benchmarks — what's the minimal hardware you recommend for initial pilot?
00:09:08 Liam: for 3B models, A100 40GB or equivalent is ideal for fp16; for int8 you can use T4-class or A10G with batch tuning. We'll run cross-hardware tests and flag any kernel mismatches.

00:09:40 Maya: note that some open models behave poorly with naive quant; part of the pipeline is calibration and a short eval to detect hallucination spikes.

00:10:05 Tom: regarding listing metadata — do we need to include quant info in the marketplace tile? like which variants are supported and cost delta?
00:10:14 Maya: yes include supported quant variants, approximate per-token cost, and model SLOs. We'll provide a recommended description template.

00:10:40 Speaker 3 (maybe Priya): we should also decide manifest signing TTLs and how to revoke.
00:10:50 Nina: revocation is mandatory for us, we need a clear key rotation and manifest revocation workflow documented.

00:11:20 Liam: another technical note: prefix caching / KV cache - for stateful chat you need warm up steps to prime the KV cache. We'll add recommended warmup RPCs in the runbook.
00:11:38 Carlos: what about cold starts when you scale from zero?
00:11:44 Liam: we recommend a warm pool or pre-warm hooks for market listing demos. Cold starts could add ~200-800ms depending on model and host. Quant sometimes reduces memory so cold starts are slightly faster.

00:12:12 Ava: telemetry endpoints — we'll want to ship traces to our internal tracing and an exported metrics feed to our Prometheus. Can Redwood push to a pull endpoint?
00:12:24 Maya: yes, we support pushing to your observability endpoints or exporting metrics via a metrics export URL; we'll include examples.

00:12:55 Tom: any blockers on the compliance side for marketplace listing?
00:13:02 Nina: primary is KMS key ownership and audit logs. We need proof of encryption keys and access logs. Also SOC2 report copy.
00:13:14 Maya: we'll attach SOC2 + ISO package in the follow-up.

00:13:40 Liam: back to benchmarks — propose the following test matrix: 3B fp16 (A100), 3B int8 (A100 + T4), 7B fp16 (A100), and a stress-run with 200 concurrent requests for 10 minutes. We'll produce CSV outputs for latency and throughput.
00:14:05 Carlos: can you also include token cost per 1k tokens? That helps procurement.
00:14:10 Liam: yes we'll calculate unit economics with recommended batching profiles.

00:14:35 Maya: small aside — we have a marketplace compliance checkbox list: SSO, KMS, manifest signing, runbook, SLA language, sample billing estimate. I'll send that checklist.

00:15:00 Tom: what about the UI tile — we may want a separate tile for quantized variants or a single tile with variants dropdown. Your recommendation?
00:15:10 Priya: variants dropdown is typical. Keep the marketplace tile minimal and link to a docs page that lists quantization caveats.

00:15:30 Ava: integration runtime - if we go private, do we still need to expose any inbound endpoints?
00:15:38 Maya: for Private with VPC peering, you keep all endpoints internal; for marketplace listing there's normally a managed proxy that facilitates billing and listing metadata while traffic can remain private. We'll document patterns.

00:16:05 Carlos: I want to flag possible latency sensitivity for a route that does real-time agent decisions. Can we have hybrid routing with sub-50ms requirement?
00:16:16 Liam: sub-50ms is tough for large context models over network. For strict sub-50 we'd recommend local edge microserving or smaller optimized model. We'll include guidance on model selection and distillation options.

00:17:00 Tom: any references or cookbooks you can share?
00:17:06 Maya: yes links: marketplace runbook template - https://redwood.ai/runbooks/marketplace-listing-template, manifest signing guide - https://redwood.ai/ops/manifest-signing, benchmark playbook - https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/quant-pipeline (note: sample links).

00:17:40 Priya: ok let's walk through a draft runbook outline — show owners and gates.
00:17:46 Liam: gate 1: security review (Nina + Redwood security), gate 2: quant benchmark pass (3B int8 p95 <= baseline*1.2), gate 3: canary run success for 48h with quality metrics within threshold.
00:18:10 Carlos: who's approving gate 2? engineering lead?
00:18:14 Maya: default is OrbitFlow eng lead (Carlos) + Redwood SE sign-off. We'll note that as configurable in the runbook.

00:18:40 Ava: question about telemetry names — can we standardize - like redwood.request.latency_ms and redwood.kv.cache_hit?
00:18:50 Liam: yes we'll include a suggested metric namespace.

00:19:10 Tom: one last deep technical: are there known failure modes when you quantize some of the open LLMs in our stack?
00:19:22 Liam: yes — some models show tokenization skew or token-prediction drift after aggressive int8; common fixes: more calibration data, per-channel quant, or keep certain sensitive layers in fp16 (mixed quant). We'll capture per-model notes in appendix.

00:20:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay recap — we have actions: benchmark runs, runbook draft, SSO/KMS artifacts, schedule tabletop. Anything else?
00:20:12 Carlos: also please include a small proof-of-concept demo script for the marketplace listing flow.
00:20:18 Maya: yes will add demo playbook.

00:20:35 Ava: will Redwood provide sample policy YAML for canary rollout config?
00:20:40 Liam: yes sample policy YAML and Helm snippets - also we'll include an example of canary config with automatic revert conditions.

00:21:05 Tom: can you add a short checklist for procurement with rough cost bands?
00:21:12 Maya: yes AE will prepare a 3-band cost estimate (dev/pilot/prod).

00:21:45 Priya: last note: we'll include a short section about governance and how to surface regressions — alerts, dashboards, and eval sets.

00:22:05 -- short lull --
00:25:00 Maya: jumping ahead a bit, do you have any hard date constraints for the listing?
00:25:07 Carlos: we'd like it live in marketplace before their next partner expo (week of 2026-01-20) ideally. So dec/Jan timeline is tight.
00:25:20 Maya: that timeline works if benchmarks and runbook move fast; we'll prioritize the checklist and benchmark slots.

00:26:10 Ava: whether we sign manifests with Cosign + KMS will depend on legal review. Nina will confirm.

00:27:00 Nina: one more compliance ask: we need a sample audit trail showing key usage - will Redwood provide a sample?
00:27:10 Maya: yes we'll produce a redwood audit sample artifact and describe fields.

00:28:30 Liam: operational note — we'll include a small script to pre-warm KV cache using a representative conv history, and a load generator playbook to simulate p95 traffic for canary.

00:29:45 Tom: okay that's helpful.

00:30:10 Maya: wrapping up, I'll send the checklist + runbook draft by Wednesday 2025-12-10, Liam will share bench results by 2025-12-15 and we'll reconvene for the tabletop on 2025-12-18.
00:30:30 Carlos: sounds good. Thanks all.
00:30:40 Maya: thanks everyone, ending early; follow-up notes will include links and action owners.

--- End transcript (trimming conversation after 30:30 for clarity though meeting continued for Q&A and scheduling notes)

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors (e.g., Speaker 2/3), minor mis-hearings like "KV cash" instead of KV cache, "notarize" sometimes transcribed as "nota rise".
